must: Five revenue models: **web catalog, digital content, advertising-supported, ad–subscription mixed, fee-based**. They work for both B2C and B2B.
**Product catalog management**: high-quality, consistent product data across **all channels**. Four benefits: organised catalog, consistent information, better customer experience, business growth.
**Multi-channel** = many channels, **not integrated**. **Omni-channel** = all channels **connected**, with one seamless experience and unified data.
Digital content: **freemium** (Spotify), **subscription** (Netflix: loyal users, predictable revenue), sponsorships, CPC, **affiliate** (30–70% commission).
**AdWords** = the advertiser pays; **AdSense** = the publisher earns per click. Ads alone pay only with a **very large audience**.
Design for success: **first impression, UX (navigation, CTAs, mobile), consistent brand, colour palette, stand out**. Design for your **target audience**.
formulas: Design stats: **75%** judge credibility by design; **94%** of B2B buyers search online first
traps: Being on Shopee + Instagram with separate stock and data is **multi**, not omni.
AdSense ≠ AdWords: the **publisher** earns vs the **advertiser** pays.
An own website does **not** automatically get traffic; it needs up-front marketing (SEO, ads).
likely: Explain the five revenue models with examples.
Risks of selling on only one platform.

story.problem: A website alone earns nothing, and selling online means competing with everyone.
story.fix: Pick a revenue model, sell across connected channels, manage the catalog and design for the target audience.
story.next: Once it sells, how do you actually run the business day to day without the owner doing everything?

terms.def: How a business earns money from its online activities.
Selling products listed in an online version of a printed catalog.
Keeping product data organised, standardised and consistent across every sales channel.
Selling on many channels that are not integrated with each other.
All channels connected, with unified data and one seamless customer experience.
A free ad-supported tier plus a paid premium tier (e.g. Spotify).
Recurring payments for ongoing access (e.g. Netflix); loyal users, predictable revenue.
Promoting another company's product via a link and earning a commission (30–70%) on sales.
Lets publishers show Google ads on their site and earn per click.
A button or link telling the visitor what to do next, e.g. 'Add to cart'.
